To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) preference matching and recommendation set size affect the persuasiveness of web personalization in the central route, (2) preference matching and sorting cue affect the persuasivness of web personalization through peripheral route, (3) preference matching and set size affect the perceived ease of use of web personalization, (4) need for cognition moderates the effects of preference matching and set sizes in the central route.

(a) the effect of personalization on persuasion depends on the level of preference matching and the need for cognition of the customer; (b) the effect of recommendation set size depends on the level preference matching and the sorting cue; (c) the effect of sorting cue depends on the level and size of recommendation set.

the effect of web personalization on customer satisfaction and purchase intention is mediated by the level of preference matching between the recommendation set and the customer, and the effect of the preference matching is moderated by the need for cognition of the customer.
